headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said the current sell-off in AI shares will pass because AI will change every industry and country.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a leading AI executive speaks on the record during a market rout, but it is a prediction by an interested party.
importance_line: Investors in AI and chip shares, including people whose pensions hold them, hear reassurance from the head of the biggest AI chip seller, but Huang runs the company that sells the chips, his view is a prediction, and shares and some AI firms' bonds are still under pressure.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, the biggest seller of AI chips, told Bloomberg's Emily Chang at an event in Berlin that "all of this is going to pass" because AI will be "transformative" for every industry and country, and called recent market news "choppy" but not a change to the fundamentals. His comments follow eight straight daily falls in the Philadelphia semiconductor index, the longest losing streak since 2008, and a drop of about a quarter this week in the shares of CoreWeave, a cloud-computing firm backed by Nvidia whose bonds recently reached levels that typically signal distress.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (HTTP 403); text read in The Straits Times, which carries the Bloomberg article. Url is the Bloomberg original named by the pool item. The day of the interview is not stated; Bloomberg's article is dated 16 Oct 2026.
